gen-dafont-dogica-gf-karla: Karla reads modern and friendly, a plain sans with a gaping c opening and a middle band tall enough to look stocky. And Dogica is the one with the muscle, heavy and widely tracked, while Karla does the quiet, approachable work of carrying sentences.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-kedebideri: Approachable is the first thing Kedebideri says, with rounded letters that stay open and a skyward x-height. Kedebideri then sits under Dogica's heavy, widely tracked display lines like an easy answer to a loud question.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-khula: Modern and neutral, Khula has a tall midsection and curves that hold their mouths open, so it feels light on the eye. And Dogica's heavy, wide-spaced lowercase gives way to that sans-serif without a fight, letting a long passage move along smoothly.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-krub: Chunky, wide and unmistakably loud. Krub, with its pronounced x-height, does the contemporary plain sans job of reading smoothly, while Dogica's heavy, commanding display letters take care of announcing.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-kufam: Kufam draws one fixed nib width, like a neon sign tube, with generously open curves in its e. Dogica brings low-contrast heft above it.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-lexend: Heavy blocks over open, outsized lowercase: Dogica's wirelike strokes of one thickness meet Lexend's curves that stay wide open. Dogica commands attention, and Lexend, a plain sans, simply keeps things approachable.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-lexend-deca: Dogica's lowercase climbs nearly to capital height, wide-tracked and heavy. Its job is to command, while Lexend Deca, a sans-serif with unshaded lines and big lowercase, quietly takes over the explaining.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-liter: Liter has no stroke contrast at all, just tall lowercase and wide mouths on its round forms. Dogica commands with its heavy, wide-tracked weight, and Liter, a sans-serif, keeps the text moving with a modern, professional hand.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-mada: Wide, weighty and a bit blunt, with Mada's curves that refuse to close sitting under it. A long stretch of Mada reads as approachable and modern, its towering midzone keeping every sans-serif line easy to follow.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-martel-sans: Big, boxy, wide-spaced heft up top. Dogica commands the page with that weight, and Martel Sans, a plain sans with generous curve openings and a high mean line, gives the eye somewhere to settle.
